50:2.4.1.text: Gull. The east end. The far end is a real place.
50:2.4.1.when: When: The player arrives in Gull's east bay holding the lock-2 keys (the far end inks; bible 5.3.4)

50:2.4.2.text: A white stone on a stump at the dam. His sign.
50:2.4.2.when: When: They see the white stone and the stone is understood

50:2.4.3.text: That pipe at the dam is drill rod. Somebody set it there for a canoe.
50:2.4.3.when: When: They hold Tauno's crew-gear talk and see the rod in fall

50:2.4.4.text: He set the same stone under the paddle at Pietro. Same hand.
50:2.4.4.when: When: They have seen the paddle-stone at Pietro and land here

50:8.4.1.text: Morning. Just waiting on a friend.

50:8.4.3.text: I don't go in the water.

50:9.1.c3.text: [Say nothing. Set the cans on the tailgate.]

50:9.1.2.text: 'Re: Haapala, E.' 'If he persists, D.S. will handle it.' Six weeks before.

50:9.1.3.text: This doesn't say who was on the lake that morning. I want you to know I know that. It says enough.

50:9.1.c4.text: There was a note on top.

50:9.1.4.text: Keep that. That's not evidence. That's his.

50:9.1.5.text: Who wrote me in 2019? The letter, Ely postmark. I need the source. I'm not asking where. I'm asking who.

50:9.1.7.text: Then that's the story. The man who wrote me, the canoe on the wrong shore, the men who watched him. His name goes in. Once it's in print, it's in print.

50:9.1.c8.text: Somebody who knew the family. That's all I can give you.

50:9.1.9.text: A source who knew the Haapala family. Bill's box carries '77. It's thinner. It'll hold.

50:9.1.10.text: Okay. Neither do I. We'll say that.

50:9.1.11.text: Go home. Sleep in a bed. I'll call your counter when it's running. You did the hard part. I just type.

50:9.1.14.text: I'd have paid you. You know that? Whatever it was.

50:9.1.17.text: Somebody called the paper about a pack and two cans. Maggie Tomczak, the Ledger. That you?

50:9.1.18.text: Fifty years I watched that lot for him.
50:9.1.18.if: to nobody, or to the player if they are near the porch

50:9.2.1.text: Two hundred fifty thousand. Twenty-five today, here. The rest as consulting fees, a little every time you come out of the woods. That's how legal wanted it. I don't know why. I think it's a tax thing.

50:9.2.2.text: Old exploration data. Company property. A liability if it comes out wrong, is what they tell me. I believe them. You think I shouldn't?

50:9.2.3.text: And nobody goes looking for the old fella any more. Wherever he is. That one's on me.

50:9.2.c7.if: to Maggie's wagon or the bench; nobody stops the player.

50:9.2.4.text: Thank you. Did you read them?
50:9.2.4.if: holding out his hand; the heavy gold ring

50:9.2.5.text: Then you know what it cost.

50:9.2.7.text: You knew the station numbers. And you came to us anyway. First sensible thing anybody near that family's done in fifty years.

50:9.2.8.text: It's only old paper. But it's ours. Walt was the best line-cutter I ever had.

50:11.1.text: Hey, so, this came for you. I think? It says 'To the one with my tent.' That's you, right? There's no name on it. There's a little drawing. Canada. Atikokan. Do you know anybody in Atikokan?

50:11.4.text: Two cups this morning. Drank both.
50:11.4.when: Ending: Journalist, Walt kept out of print

50:11.5.text: Saw my name in the paper. Moving on before the snow. Glad it's out.

50:11.6.text: Saw they got their permit. Hope it bought you something good. Keep your canoe close.

50:12.3.c1.text: I found this on top of them.

50:12.3.1.text: Eighth of August. Sawbill. You're buying.

50:12.3.2.text: I wanted the mine. I still want the mine. Now it's a fair fight.

50:12.3.4.text: I wanted the mine. Not like this. They're building it on a lie, and they paid you for the lie.

50:12.3.5.text: Thank you. I'm sorry. Both. — D.
50:12.3.5.when: *Turned:* journalist: he sends a card to the home counter

50:12.3.6.text: I read it. The paper. I read it in the car three times.

50:12.3.7.text: Somebody talked, back then. I always thought somebody talked.

50:12.3.8.text: I hope it was a lot.
50:12.3.8.when: *Money:* if the player talks to her again

50:12.3.9.text: Somebody left an old Grumman at the {landing}. Boss says it's ours now. It's loud but it's basically indestructible.
50:12.3.9.if: Only if the player used the Grumman; it goes on the home rental rack, and from then on now and then a family party is seen paddling it: "Some kid'll need it someday."

50:12.4.1.text: Paper says the papers were in the woods somewhere back of Bald Eagle. Didn't say where. I'm not asking where. If there was anything else back there. A building, say. Is it history or junk? I'm supposed to know which.

50:12.4.2.text: Okay. I never heard about it.

50:12.4.3.text: Then tell me where, sometime, and I'll come with a crew.
